ledger.claim: The rider's only message on this trip is a locating and coordinating message of exactly the kind POL-NS-04(a) names. Sent at 10:44:14 from her device and delivered at 10:44:15, its text is "im at the pickup, cant see you" - she states that she is at the pickup point and that she cannot see the vehicle. Neither the rider's own position nor her inability to see the car is in doubt on the face of the message, so limb (a) is satisfied on the chat record itself.

Limb (b) is satisfied on the driver's own telemetry. The chat log holds one message and it is the rider's: the driver posted no reply within 120 seconds of it, and in truth no reply at all, because the message was never opened (read_at is null) and the log closes at 10:44:14. trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so no in-app voice call was placed at any point before he terminated the trip at 10:50:57 - 403 seconds after the message and 443 seconds after his own arrival tap at 10:43:34. His statement "Waited the full period" is consistent with the GPS but is silent on the message. On this record the coordination failure was the driver's: he held position for more than seven minutes and never read or answered the rider's one attempt to make contact.

Limb (c) cannot be run, and I do not ask the Judge to find it satisfied. The gps_trace carries no rider track at all: rider_presence.available is false and rider_fix_count is 0, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is UNDECIDABLE and neutral under POL-NS-11 - the test could not be run, and the Judge must say so rather than inferring that the rider was elsewhere. POL-NS-04's own text calls the artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(b) for that limb, while POL-NS-11 provides that the missing rider_track is not the evidence of any deciding fact for the driver's clauses and does not by itself engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e); the rider accepts POL-NS-11 and relies on it only for this neutral-treatment point. The absence of her track is a capture failure on the platform's side, and it is not an act or omission of the rider. On that footing POL-NS-04 does not by itself carry a refund here, and the rider does not put her case on it.

I take the arithmetic as the driver's track gives it, so that the only live issue is a narrow one. The longest qualifying in-geofence run is 440 seconds of continuous fixes from 10:43:34 to 10:50:54, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix as POL-NS-01(c) directs and not from the arrival tap, and the free waiting period in force for this trip is the 180 seconds carried in trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. The rider does not contest limb (c) on those numbers and no shortfall arises under POL-NS-06; her case is not that the driver waited too briefly, but that he waited without ever opening the one message she sent him.

The single advisory artifact in this bundle is MISSING: EV-ADVIS-02758-01 carries no payload and admissibility.weight_multiplier 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, "No advisory covers Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru in this window." I disclose that weight and that issue code as POL-GEN-02(1) requires, and I cite the absence for no more than it is worth: because no advisory covers the pickup road, the driver has no POL-NS-06(i) accumulation available to him out of any kerb restriction, enforcement operation, closure or accident, and nothing in this record suggests that holding position at the pin was ever unlawful or impossible for him.

POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are both made out on this record. The trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-08-16T10:43:34+08:00, and the driver's own GPS trace independently places him inside the STANDARD arrival radius at that very second: the derived arrival block reports 45 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a dwell_start_offset_sec of 0.0, so the first qualifying in-geofence fix coincides with the tap rather than trailing it. There is no gap between the platform's arrival event and the driver's measured presence at the pin.

The free waiting period was served in full. The driver held position inside the geofence for a single continuous run of 440 seconds, from 10:43:34 to 10:50:54, across 45 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps. The period in force for this trip is trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 seconds, and the derived shortfall is -260 seconds, i.e. a surplus of 260 seconds over the minimum, so POL-NS-01(c) is satisfied with room to spare. It is satisfied even against the 300-second STANDARD figure in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec, which under the resolution_rule is retained only to interpret records authored before policy version 2. The run continues until 10:50:54, so the driver was still holding the pickup roughly 400 seconds after the rider's own 10:44:14 message: the wait was served after contact, not exhausted before it.

POL-NS-01(d) is satisfied in full. The trip was terminated by the driver at 2026-08-16T10:50:57+08:00 — 443 seconds after the first qualifying in-geofence fix — with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the clause recognises. The record shows no boarding event anywhere, and platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null, so there is no longer threshold the cancellation had to reach.

The rider's exoneration clause does not reach him. POL-NS-04 requires all three limbs. Limb (a) is made out: the rider's single message at 10:44:14 reads 'im at the pickup, cant see you'. Limb (b) is made out: the driver neither replied nor placed an in-app call, trip_record.in_app_calls being empty. But limb (c) cannot be run at all — the gps_trace carries no rider track (rider_presence.available = false, rider_fix_count = 0), so there is no admissible fix by which the rider's device could be placed within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius. POL-NS-11 fixes the consequence: limb (c) is UNDECIDABLE and neutral, POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider, and the dispute is decided on the driver's own evidence. I do not ask the Judge to infer the rider was elsewhere; I ask it to record, as POL-NS-11 directs, that the test could not be run. The absent rider track does not impair the driver's trace for arrival or dwell and does not engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e).

POL-NS-05 does not bite. The clause fires only where the 'arrived' event places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or shows him travelling at 15 km/h or more. On the derived facts the driver is inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from the exact timestamp the arrived event carries, dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0 and longest_qualifying_run.first_ts equal to arrived_at, so the marker is corroborated rather than contradicted. And even if the marker were treated as false and the clock recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, limb (iii) applies: the corrected dwell of 440 seconds still meets the 180-second minimum, the false marker would not by itself defeat the fee, and POL-NS-01 governs the outcome.

POL-NS-03 has no application. That clause governs a driver who was stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin — a wrong-face-of-the-venue case. Here the driver's qualifying stationary fixes fall inside the 50 m STANDARD radius itself (qualifying_fix_count 45, longest qualifying run 440 seconds), so there is no wrong-entrance case to answer and no pin-ambiguity goodwill question arises. The clause's 400 m ceiling is never reached because the 50 m test is already met.

POL-NS-06 does not fire either. Its trigger is an effective in-geofence dwell shorter than the free waiting period, and the derived shortfall_sec here is -260 — a surplus of 260 seconds over the 180-second minimum, not a shortfall. The dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence interval, so the accumulation across separate intervals that POL-NS-06(i) permits is not needed and its absent conditions (leash, advisory type, populated advisory) are irrelevant.

EV-ADVIS-02758-01 is MISSING: no traffic advisory covers Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru in this window. Its admissibility status is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I disclose that plainly. The driver relies on it for nothing and cites it only to close the point: with a MISSING and unpopulated advisory, POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable to either side — no party can invoke it to accumulate separate in-geofence intervals or to excuse anything. The driver's dwell is one continuous 440-second run that needs no accumulation, so this absence costs the driver nothing.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force. platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd is 4.50 and the fare breakdown's derived money block states driver_compensation of 3.60 under POL-NS-07; that reconciled figure is the payout. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the 4 the clause requires, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d (70) is 0.0, far below the 0.08 rate. Both limbs must hold and neither does, so compensation is paid rather than withheld. Those two fields are the only profile fields I cite, exactly as POL-GEN-01 prescribes for this test.

The ruling value this record produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, not NO_ACTION. On the fee itself the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the 4.50 charge stays where it is. But POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-03 require that where compensation is paid the emitted ruling be DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at 3.60 — the amount of money the ruling moves, not a refund to the filing party.

No POL-NS-09 trigger is present, so the case should not be pulled to human review and the fee should not be left on hold. Nothing in the record contradicts itself on arrival, dwell or termination — the trip_record events and the gps_trace agree on the arrival second. Limb (c) is not met: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so there is no repeat-dispute pattern. Limb (d) is not met: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0. Limb (e) is not met either: POL-NS-11 states that the absent rider track is not the evidence for the deciding fact of the driver's clauses and does not impair the gps_trace for arrival or dwell. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts here — trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown, chat log — is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) confidence cap cannot force escalation.

ruling.explanation:
The no-show charge stands, and the driver is paid. The ride record and the driver's GPS trace agree on everything that matters. The driver tapped 'arrived' at 10:43:34, and the GPS trace independently places him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius from that same second (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0; 45 qualifying in-geofence fixes). He then held position continuously for 440 seconds, from 10:43:34 to 10:50:54. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, so he waited 260 seconds longer than the minimum. He terminated the trip at 10:50:57 with the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after that period had run, and the record shows no boarding. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 are therefore satisfied. The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: it is corroborated by a fix inside the radius at the tap second (no >300 m distance and no 15 km/h motion), and even on a recomputed clock the 440-second dwell still clears the 180-second minimum. POL-NS-03 has no application because the driver was inside the radius, not merely within 400 m of the pin, and POL-NS-06 does not fire because there is no shortfall (the derived figure is a 260-second surplus). The rider's argument is POL-NS-04, and it fails on its own terms: limbs (a) and (b) are met (she sent 'im at the pickup, cant see you' at 10:44:14, the driver never replied within 120 seconds and never placed an in-app call, trip_record.in_app_calls being empty), but limb (c) cannot be run at all because the GPS trace carries no rider track (rider_presence.available is false, rider_fix_count 0). Under POL-NS-11 that limb is undecidable and neutral: I do not infer the rider was elsewhere, but POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate her, and the fee is decided on the driver's own evidence. The driver's payout is fixed by POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the 4.50 fee, which is the 3.60 stated in the fare breakdown's money block; the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, and 0 of 70 completed trips is 0.0, both below the clause's thresholds). On the fee itself the rider's claim is not supported: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the 4.50 charge stays as it is. Because the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, amount_sgd carries the same 3.60 figure as driver_compensation_sgd, per POL-GEN-03. The single traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02758-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and is relied on by nobody; its absence costs the driver nothing because his dwell is one unbroken interval needing no accumulation. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the fee, no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is present (no contradicting artifacts, no repeat-dispute pattern, no anti-farming trip, no impaired sole evidence), and the monetary effect of 3.60 does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of 8.00, so it executes automatically. No referral is produced, since POL-NS-05(ii) is not engaged by a corroborated marker.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
